they-dont-listen.name: Being heard
they-dont-listen.line: The people in charge don't listen to people like me.
they-dont-listen.why: Keeps the same complaint but says it the way people do ("they don't listen"), and the name says what is missing instead of the civics word "Representation".

democracy-slipping.name: Democracy
democracy-slipping.line: I worry our democracy is slowly slipping away.
democracy-slipping.why: The ID names democracy slipping, but the current line drifted to institutions in general; this brings it back to what the pain is about, calmly and without doom.

democracy-slipping.name: Institutions
democracy-slipping.line: I see courts, elections and a free press being worn down.
democracy-slipping.why: Keeps the broader institutions framing but names which ones, so the line is something a person can picture rather than an abstraction.

corruption.name: Money in politics
corruption.line: I see the rules bend for people with money.
corruption.why: Every other name under Government is an area (Taxes, Voting, Local control); "Corruption" is the only problem label, and this area name keeps the same line.

taxes-dont-buy-much.name: Taxes
taxes-dont-buy-much.line: I pay more in taxes and get less back in services.
taxes-dont-buy-much.why: The current line never says what is paid or what comes back; naming taxes and services makes it clear on its own.

far-away-decisions.name: Local control
far-away-decisions.line: Decisions about my town get made by people far away.
far-away-decisions.why: "Decisions about here" reads awkwardly; "my town" is how a person would say it out loud.

immigration-broken.name: Immigration
immigration-broken.line: I see an immigration system that's broken, and nobody fixes it.
immigration-broken.why: The current line is hedged ("I don't think... working well"); this says it plainly, matches the ID, and people on any side of the debate could say it.

pairs.distinction: Not being heard is about my voice being ignored by any official; local control is about where decisions get made, even by people who might listen.
pairs.reason: Someone ignored by their own city council and someone whose town is run from the state capital name different problems and would each pick one easily.

pairs.distinction: Freedoms is my own choices being taken away; democracy slipping is the shared system of courts, elections and press weakening.
pairs.reason: People who feel personally restricted and people worried about the system as a whole often aren't the same people, so both need a place to say it.

pairs.distinction: Accountability is leaders breaking promises and facing nothing; corruption is the rules bending for people with money.
pairs.reason: A broken campaign promise and a rich donor getting special treatment are different complaints, and the lines already say which is which.

pairs.distinction: Taxes is about what I pay and what I get for it; accountability is about leaders getting away with broken promises.
pairs.reason: Paying more for worse services is a money complaint that someone could have even with honest leaders, so the two don't blur.

pairs.distinction: Accountability is individual leaders facing no consequences; democracy slipping is the institutions themselves being worn down.
pairs.reason: One is about people in power and the other about the system that should hold them, and the reworded democracy line makes that clearer.

pairs.distinction: Not being heard is my own voice ignored today; democracy slipping is the system that guarantees that voice weakening over time.
pairs.reason: Feeling ignored by officials is common even where democracy is stable, so a person can easily tell which of the two they mean.

pairs.distinction: Infrastructure is the roads, water and power I depend on breaking down; taxes is the sense of paying more for less across the board.
pairs.reason: Crumbling roads are a concrete daily problem whether or not someone thinks about taxes, and a person can choose between them without thinking twice.

pairs.distinction: Infrastructure is things that exist but keep breaking; car-or-nothing is having no way to get around except driving.
pairs.reason: Potholes and water main breaks are a different problem from having no bus or sidewalk at all, so they belong in separate pains and groups.

pairs.distinction: Voting is about the choice in front of me at election time; misinformation is not trusting what I read about anything.
pairs.reason: Someone can trust the news and still not know which candidate fits them, so the two pains name different moments.

nobody-covers-here.name: No local news
nobody-covers-here.line: Nobody reports on my town any more, so I don't know what's going on here.
nobody-covers-here.why: Brings back what the ID names (no one covering here) and says why the person doesn't know, while the problem-style name matches Misinformation if the founder wants one style for the heading.

nobody-covers-here.name: Local news
nobody-covers-here.line: Nobody reports on what's happening in my town any more.
nobody-covers-here.why: Keeps the current name and the plain everyday sentence, but points at the missing coverage rather than the person's own not knowing.

watched-by-companies.name: Being tracked
watched-by-companies.line: I feel watched by companies that know everything about me.
watched-by-companies.why: Same line; the problem-style name says what is wrong, so the heading no longer mixes Misinformation (a problem) with Privacy (an area).

dont-know-whats-true.name: Knowing what's true
dont-know-whats-true.line: I don't know what's true any more.
dont-know-whats-true.why: Same line; an area-style name matching Local news and Privacy, the other way to give the heading one style.

pairs.distinction: Misinformation is about not trusting what you read and hear about anything; Voting is about choosing between candidates, which can be hard even with good information.
pairs.reason: Someone can trust the news and still not know who to vote for, so a person can choose between these without thinking twice.

pairs.distinction: Local news is about no one reporting what goes on in town; Coordination is about not finding the people already working on a cause you care about.
pairs.reason: One is missing news about the town and the other is missing allies for a cause, and the line wording already keeps them apart.

pairs.distinction: Privacy is the societal worry about companies collecting data on everyone; Scams is a personal loss of money to a fraud.
pairs.reason: Losing money to a scammer and feeling tracked by companies are different experiences on different pages, and neither is a version of the other.

nothing-ever-changes.name: Progress
nothing-ever-changes.line: I keep seeing the same problems year after year, and nothing changes.
nothing-ever-changes.why: Keeps the year-after-year feeling, says the 'nothing changes' the ID names, and swaps the problem label Gridlock for an area label like the rest of the heading.

nothing-ever-changes.name: Change
nothing-ever-changes.line: Nothing ever seems to change where I live, no matter how bad things get.
nothing-ever-changes.why: Says the pain the way people put it out loud, grounded in where the person lives.

groups-go-nowhere.name: Groups
groups-go-nowhere.line: The groups I'm part of talk a lot and never get anything done.
groups-go-nowhere.why: Covers boards, clubs and committees, not only meetings, and says what goes wrong: talk without action.

shouting-into-void.name: Speaking up
shouting-into-void.line: I speak up about what I care about, and it feels like shouting into the void.
shouting-into-void.why: Says what the person did and what came back, using the everyday phrase the ID names, and makes the name an area label like the rest of the heading.

shouting-into-void.name: Being heard
shouting-into-void.line: I call, write and post about what matters to me, and nothing comes back.
shouting-into-void.why: Concrete about the effort, so it reads apart from Gridlock (the world not changing) and Helping (not knowing what to do).

alone-in-caring.name: Allies
alone-in-caring.line: I feel alone in caring about this where I live.
alone-in-caring.why: Names the loneliness the ID describes, which separates it from Coordination (finding existing efforts).

pairs.distinction: Gridlock is about problems in the world staying put; Unheard is about my own effort getting no response.
pairs.reason: Someone who has never spoken up can feel stuck problems, and someone who speaks up can feel unheard even on things that are moving.

pairs.distinction: Meetings is about the groups I'm in; Gridlock is about the place I live.
pairs.reason: A person stuck in a talk-only committee picks a different card than a person watching the same potholes for ten years.

pairs.distinction: Giving is about money and not knowing if it works; Unheard is about voice and getting no response.
pairs.reason: Doubting where a donation of money goes and feeling ignored after speaking up are different experiences with different fixes.

pairs.distinction: Allies is about not finding others who care; Unheard is about my effort going nowhere.
pairs.reason: One is about company and the other about results, so a person can tell at a glance which one is theirs.

pairs.distinction: Allies is about finding people who share a cause; Neighbors is about not knowing the people on my street at all.
pairs.reason: Someone can know every neighbor and still feel alone in caring about an issue, and the other way round.

pairs.distinction: Coordination is the practical search for existing efforts and groups; Allies is the feeling of being the only one who cares.
pairs.reason: They sit close, but the sharper Allies line (feeling alone) makes the choice easy against Coordination (can't find who's already working on it).

pairs.distinction: Coordination is about finding who is already working on a cause; Local news is about knowing what is going on in town.
pairs.reason: The Coordination wording has moved from its ID toward finding existing efforts, which is what keeps it apart from Local news.

pairs.distinction: Helping is not knowing what to do; Allies is not knowing who else cares.
pairs.reason: What to do and who to do it with are different gaps, and people usually know which one they have.

pairs.distinction: Helping is before acting; Unheard is after acting with nothing to show for it.
pairs.reason: A person who hasn't started and a person who tried and got nothing would not mistake one card for the other.

pairs.distinction: Helping is about time and action; Giving is about money and whether it works.
pairs.reason: Both start with 'I'd', but one is about doing and the other about paying, so they lead to different fixes.

pairs.distinction: Volunteers is the organizer's view of a thin bench; Helping is the would-be helper's view.
pairs.reason: They are two sides of the same gap, and each side would pick its own card.

pairs.distinction: Volunteers is about too few people carrying the work; Meetings is about groups that don't act.
pairs.reason: A group can get plenty done on the backs of three people, or have many members and still do nothing.

pairs.distinction: Collaborators is about having a specific idea and no one to build it with; Allies is about not finding others who care.
pairs.reason: Someone with a project in hand is looking for builders, not just company.

pairs.distinction: Collaborators is about a shared idea needing a team; Creativity on the personal page is about losing time to make things at all.
pairs.reason: One is about people to build with and the other about room in my own life to make things, so they are different pains, not one pain on two pages.

at least 25,198,000 Medicaid enrollees had been disenrolled during the unwinding

leads: Founder pool (hierarchy v2), paperwork_bureaucracy: "benefits i depend on have been denied reduced or terminated", "i can t figure out how to apply for or keep benefits i need".

WHOQOL-BREF has no item on taking part in public life, and WHO/IHME cause-of-burden lists and 211 top-needs reports name nothing in this scope, so none of them gets entries here. Wikidata QIDs came from the wbsearchentities API (about 25 lookups, not counted as searches); activist burnout has no item, so compassion fatigue (Q5156139) stands in. Most outside lists measure taking part rather than pains, so several entries map to existing pains that only It's thesis named before; the list passages here (Pew, Community Life Survey, Census CEV, Give.org) are the first opened sources bearing on Representation, Unheard, Volunteers, Helping and Giving, which ingest could add as evidence.
